question: m12
q: Is electricity inflation running ahead of overall inflation?

transcript.answer:
**Yes.** Electricity prices are rising much faster than overall inflation.

- **August 2026:** electricity was up **13.2%** year on year, against **4.0%** for all groups CPI. That is a gap of about 9 percentage points.
- **Peak:** electricity hit **37.1%** in October 2025 and **37.0%** in February 2026, when all groups was running at 3.7–3.8%.
- **Recent months:** the electricity rate has eased from its early-2026 peak. It was 32.2% in January, 25.4% in March, 22.4% in June, 6.1% in July and 13.2% in August. All groups stayed between 3.5% and 4.6% over the same stretch.

The electricity figures are distorted by base effects. Electricity inflation was negative from mid-2024 to mid-2025, which I believe mainly reflected government energy bill rebates (I didn't check this against a source). When those rebates dropped out of the comparison from mid-2025, the year-on-year rate jumped. The July 2026 dip looks like another base effect, so the monthly swings are less informative than the overall trend. Even so, electricity has been running well above headline inflation for over a year.
